sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home, Lucknow And Others Counsel for Applicant :- Rajesh Kumar Awasthi

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Rakesh K. Tripathi Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. None appears on behalf of the complainant despite service of notice.

3. It is argued by the counsel for the applicant that in terms of the F.I.R., a missing person report had lodged and subsequently, in the statement under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., the victim did not support the prosecution story and stated that she had gone along with the applicant on her own will and with him for one and half months.
There was slight variance in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. wherein she alleged wrong was also committed on her.

3. Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer.
4. Considering the two statements where the victim herself has stated that she had gone along with the applicant and stayed for a substantial time, a case for bail is made out particularly when the applicant is in custody since 14.08.2022 and has no criminal history, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant- Deepu be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.330 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC & Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, Police Station Sandi, District Hardoi, on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
